title: Ops Signal: Weekly Synthesis — May 19 2029
body:
Purpose:
A concise week-in-ops synthesis: incidents, SLO posture, handoff notes, and follow-ups. Meant for quick skim by PMs, SREs, and the on-call rota.

High-level summary (May 13–19):
- Incidents: 3 customer-visible degradations (two transient, one escalated to P2).
  - Edge-cache spike (May 15 02:40 UTC): cache-eviction storm caused high p99 token latency for hosted-api /generate endpoints in us-west-2. Mitigated by temporary cache-size bump + coordinated pod restart. Root cause: KV cache compaction job overlap with peak traffic.
  - Model-conversion disruption (May 16 11:05 UTC): background quantize job throttled shared GPU scheduler, causing queueing on Dedicated pool for ~12 minutes. Autoscaler didn’t spin additional nodes fast enough because burst budget was exhausted.
  - Reranker timeout cascade (May 18 17:30 UTC): external feature store API returned 503s, triggered client-side exponential backoff but upstream retries caused queue buildup and 504s. Fallthrough policy routed to smaller model variant, reducing error surface.

SLO posture snapshot (end of week):
- Hosted API success SLO (5-min rolling): target 99.95% -> observed 99.87% (error budget burned ~0.08% this week).
- Median latency (p50) stable at 85ms; p95 increased from 220ms -> 360ms (during edge-cache event); p99 spike to 1.6s during incident window.
- Dedicated throughput SLO: sustained throughput met except during the quantize throttle window.
- Current error budget balance (monthly window): ~0.65% remaining. Flag: if we take another P2-level degradation, we hit alert threshold for throttle of non-essential rollout changes.

On-call & handoff notes:
- Weekend coverage (May 20–21): primary = Evan Morris, secondary = Lina Ortega. Pager rules: primary first 6 hours, then escalate to secondary.
- Handoff checklist items completed: runbook link verified, API keys validated, recent playbook changes (kv-cache compaction) highlighted.
- New runbook updates required: add explicit pre-check that disables long-running compaction jobs during known traffic windows; include a shunt that temporarily routes requests to regional fallback pool. (Action: Diego to draft runbook edits, due May 24).

Action items & owners (priority-sorted):
1) Short-term: Add compaction-job guardwindow. Owner: Diego Ruiz. ETA: 2029-05-24. Linked: OPS-4921.
2) Mid-term: Adjust Dedicated autoscaler to allow emergency burst credits for quantize/compile jobs (proposal: reserve 10% burst tokens per cluster). Owner: Asha Patel + infra. ETA: proposal by 2029-06-03.
3) Observability: Add a synthetic that hits /generate with prefix patterns that exercise KV cache cold-paths; alert when p95 > 300ms for 3 consecutive minutes. Owner: Lina Ortega. ETA: 2029-05-28.
4) Customer communication: Draft short post-incident summary for impacted tenants (two accounts) — include mitigation and timeline. Owner: Evan Morris. ETA: 2029-05-21.

Notes from incident retrospectives (what worked / what didn’t):
- What worked:
  - Fallback routing to smaller model variant reduced total error exposure during reranker timeout cascade. Good guardrail.
  - Runbook escalation flow was largely followed; on-call handoff was clean.
- What didn’t work:
  - Background maintenance windows overlapped with traffic spikes (compaction scheduling needs smarter boundaries).
  - Autoscaler burst logic is conservative for GPU-anchored jobs; observed slow scale-up during quantize job.
  - Some runbook steps assume manual approval from infra team which slowed mitigation by ~5 minutes — need pre-authorized emergency steps.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is it acceptable to impose a hard-disable on compaction during peak business hours? Pros: immediate reduction in p99 spikes. Cons: cache size may drift, leading to higher long-term miss-rate. (Engineering product tradeoff; input from model-ops required).
- Can we implement per-tenant compaction throttles so large tenants don’t induce global churn? (Feasibility: requires scheduler + tenant tagging).

Quick metrics dump (for debug, numbers rounded):
- Total requests (hosted-api): 14.9M/week
- Customer-facing errors: 1.8k/week (majority from retries)
- Avg tokens/sec per GPU: 12.5k (peak window 18.9k)
- Cache hit-rate global: 91.2% (dipped to 78% during cache storm)

Runbooks & links worth reading:
- kv-cache-runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/kv-cache-runbook
- dedicated-autoscale-playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Dedicated-Autoscale
- incident OPS-4921: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4921
- slack run channel: #sre-ops (bookmark pinned message with emergency steps)

FYI / low-priority notes / scratchpad:
- Idea: experiment with light-weight compaction (sample-based) to reduce eviction storms. TODO: spike investigation (2d).
- Note to self: check whether quantize jobs can be scheduled with GPU-affinity lanes to avoid pre-empting inference pools.
- Remind PMs to surface tenant growth signals that might require region-specific cache sizing.

End of synthesis. If you want a one-page for execs, I can extract TL;DR and crisp timeline.

Last edited by: Asha Patel on 2029-05-22.
